basis: Posterior cortical neurodegeneration causes visual processing deficits; definition explicitly excludes ocular abnormalities.
Isolated premature fusion of a frontosphenoidal cranial suture; skull bone disorder.
Primary meningeal melanoma with diffuse meningeal spread; CNS origin, not cutaneous melanoma.
Susceptibility to ovarian cancer; reproductive organs have no axis, and susceptibility does not establish organ damage.
Spastic ataxia and congenital fixed miosis with impaired pupillary responses define the syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in only 5-29%.
Anterior pituitary hormone deficiency defines the disorder; intellectual disability is variable, without evidence here that it affects at least 30%.
Primary uterine corpus neoplasm; reproductive organs have no axis. Mesenchymal histology does not establish locomotor tissue involvement.
Cholesterol emboli obstruct renal vessels and directly injure the kidney; both vascular and renal disease define this concept.
Localized neuroendocrine neoplasm of carotid body paraganglia; classified as both peripheral nervous system and endocrine neoplasm.
Definition describes usually asymptomatic maternal UPD9; phenotypes from unmasked recessive diseases cannot establish direct organ involvement by UPD itself.
Inherited biliary phospholipid transport defect causes progressive cholestatic liver injury; diarrhea and congestive splenomegaly do not prove additional organ damage.
Site-unspecified epithelial cancer umbrella; no organ axis applies across most subtypes, and epithelial origin alone does not identify skin involvement.
Reflex blood pressure regulation disorder; neural mediation does not establish brain or peripheral nerve damage.
Compression and stenosis of the celiac artery define the condition; gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish common direct intestinal injury.
Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma arises in urinary tract urothelium, principally bladder or renal pelvis; spindle morphology adds no muscle axis.
Defined as a KIF5A-related nervous system disorder; represented subtypes affect central motor pathways or peripheral nerves.
Secondary pigmentary retinal degeneration; retinal disease establishes the ocular axis without specifying an infectious or immune cause.
Benign immature adipose tissue tumor, usually arising in subcutis; deep or intramuscular locations do not characterize most patients.
Cerebral hypomyelination with developmental and motor impairment; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated ocular tissue disease.
Hereditary skin hyperpigmentation; no evidence supplied for disease of another organ.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by cataracts and cardiomyopathy; direct skeletal myopathy occurs in 80-99%, filling the four-axis cap.
Carcinoma in situ originates in bile duct epithelium; intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Primary oligodendroglial tumor of the spinal cord.
Inherited immunodeficiency with mycobacterial disease; anemia in 2/2 supports blood involvement. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Inhaled kaolin dust causes pulmonary pneumoconiosis; inflammatory dust injury alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
